# bayesval

Bayesian probabilistic validation of Cox proportional-hazards prediction
models. Every discrimination, calibration, and clinical-utility metric
you would normally compute once — Harrell/Uno/Gonen-Heller/Antolini
concordance, time-dependent AUC, calibration-in-the-large, calibration
slope, ICI/E50/E90, D-calibration, IPCW Brier/IBS/IPA, R²_D,
decision-curve net benefit — is instead reported as a **posterior
distribution** with a 95% credible interval.

The single idea behind the package: every validation metric `M` is a
functional `M(S, data)` of a posterior survival object and the data.
Evaluate the existing frequentist estimator at each posterior draw; the
collection of per-draw values **is** the metric’s posterior. No new
point estimators —
[`propagate_metric()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/propagate_metric.md)
is the only wrapper. Two uncertainty sources are propagated coherently:
model-parameter uncertainty (posterior draws) and evaluation-sample
uncertainty (a Bayesian bootstrap over the validation set).

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wmotte/bayesval")
```

The modelling core needs only `survival`; everything below works without
a Stan toolchain via the `coxph` backend. The full-Bayes path (`rstan`),
BART comparator (`BART`), and a few optional calibration/decision-curve
estimators are Suggested, not required — install them only if you use
that backend.

## Quick start

``` r

library(bayesval)

set.seed(1); n <- 500
dat <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rbinom(n, 1, 0.4))
dat$time   <- rexp(n, 0.15 * exp(0.8 * dat$x1 - 0.5 * dat$x2))
dat$status <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.7)
hz <- quantile(dat$time[dat$status == 1], c(.25, .5, .75))

ps <- fit_bayes_survival(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2, dat, hz,
                         backend = "coxph", S = 300)           # survival-only

disc <- propagate_many(ps, list(harrell  = metric_harrell_c,
                                uno      = metric_uno_c,
                                antolini = metric_antolini_c))
posterior_table(disc)                                          # median [95% CrI]

propagate_metric(ps, metric_harrell_c, weights = "bootstrap")  # + eval-set uncertainty
ppc_calibration(ps, horizon = 2)$ppp                            # calibration PPC
posterior_net_benefit(ps)$p_useful                              # decision-curve layer
```

## Model backends

Every backend returns the same model-agnostic `psurv` object (an
`[S x n x H]` posterior survival array plus the linear predictor), so
every metric above is backend-agnostic:

| backend | needs | role |
|----|----|----|
| `stan_pwexp` | `rstan` | **primary** full-Bayes piecewise-exponential PH (MCMC) |
| `pwexp` | `survival` | piecewise-exponential Poisson-trick PH (GLM + Laplace) |
| `coxph` | `survival` | Cox-Laplace approximation (fast fallback / no Stan) |
| `bart` | `BART` | nonparametric Bayesian survival comparator |
| `stan_surv` | `rstanarm` w/ `stan_surv` | M-spline PH (aspirational; not yet in CRAN rstanarm) |

MCMC fits are gated by
[`check_mcmc_gate()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/check_mcmc_gate.md)
(Rhat \< 1.01, ESS, no divergences) before any metric is reported;
[`prior_sensitivity()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/prior_sensitivity.md)
refits under several log-hazard-ratio prior scales to check robustness.

## Documentation

[`?propagate_metric`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/propagate_metric.md)
is the entry point for writing a new metric; every `metric_*()` function
follows the same `function(draw, w)` signature and can be passed to it
directly. See the function reference
([`help(package = "bayesval")`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/bayesval/man)) for
the full API.

## Citation and reproducibility

`bayesval` is the software companion to:

> Otte WM, Kampman SL, \[…\] *A Bayesian framework for validating
> survival prediction models: posterior credible intervals for
> discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility.* in prep.

# Package index

## Model layer

Fit a posterior survival object (psurv) from any backend

- [`fit_bayes_survival()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/fit_bayes_survival.md)
  :

  Fit a Bayesian survival model and return a `psurv`.

- [`psurv_external()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/psurv_external.md)
  : External-validation psurv: evaluate a coxph's Laplace posterior on
  NEW data.

- [`psurv_from_coxph()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/psurv_from_coxph.md)
  : Fallback constructor: posterior draws from a frequentist Cox fit.

- [`psurv_from_pwexp()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/psurv_from_pwexp.md)
  : Piecewise-exponential (Poisson-trick) Bayesian PH model -\> psurv.

- [`psurv_from_bart()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/psurv_from_bart.md)
  : BART survival (nonparametric Bayesian) model -\> psurv.

- [`psurv_from_stan_surv()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/psurv_from_stan_surv.md)
  : Build a psurv from an rstanarm::stan_surv fit (the primary Bayesian
  PH model).

- [`fit_stan_pwexp()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/fit_stan_pwexp.md)
  : Fit a full-Bayes piecewise-exponential PH model and return a rich
  object.

- [`stan_pwexp_predict()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/stan_pwexp_predict.md)
  : External-validation psurv from a fitted stan_pwexp model on new
  data.

- [`new_psurv()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/new_psurv.md)
  : Construct a posterior survival object.

- [`make_psurv_fitter()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/make_psurv_fitter.md)
  : Build a fit_psurv closure for bb_optimism(): function(data, weights)
  -\> psurv.

## MCMC diagnostics and priors

- [`check_mcmc_gate()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/check_mcmc_gate.md)
  [`mcmc_gate()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/check_mcmc_gate.md)
  : Convergence gate: TRUE only if Rhat \< max_rhat, ESS \>= min_ess, no
  divergences.

- [`mcmc_diagnostics()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/mcmc_diagnostics.md)
  : MCMC convergence diagnostics for a fitted Bayesian survival model.

- [`prior_sensitivity()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/prior_sensitivity.md)
  : Prior-sensitivity analysis (checklist 1): refit the primary
  full-Bayes PH model (fit_stan_pwexp) under several log-HR prior SDs
  and compare the posterior of each validation metric. A robust
  conclusion should be stable across weakly-informative priors; a large
  shift flags prior-dependence.

- [`loo_survival()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/loo_survival.md)
  :

  PSIS-LOO elpd from a pointwise log-likelihood matrix `[S x n]`.

## Caching

- [`fit_bayes_survival_cached()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/fit_bayes_survival_cached.md)
  : Fit a psurv with transparent disk caching.
- [`psurv_cache_key()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/psurv_cache_key.md)
  : Deterministic cache key for a psurv fit from its defining inputs.
- [`save_psurv()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/save_psurv.md)
  : Save a psurv to disk (creates the directory).
- [`load_psurv()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/load_psurv.md)
  : Load a psurv from disk (validates the class).
- [`clear_psurv_cache()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/clear_psurv_cache.md)
  : Remove cached psurv files.

## Uncertainty propagation

The one idea — propagate any frequentist estimator across the posterior

- [`propagate_metric()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/propagate_metric.md)
  : Propagate a per-draw metric across the posterior (B2), optionally
  with the Bayesian bootstrap (B3).

- [`propagate_many()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/propagate_many.md)
  : Convenience: propagate several named metric functions in one pass
  over the draws (cheaper than one pass each — the survival object is
  only sliced once).

- [`propagate_bootstrap()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/propagate_bootstrap.md)
  : Propagate a metric with the Bayesian bootstrap (B2 + B3 in one
  call). Thin alias for propagate_metric(..., weights = "bootstrap").

- [`posterior_table()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/posterior_table.md)
  :

  Format a posterior_metric (or several) as a median `[95% CrI]` table.

- [`posterior_vs_frequentist()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/posterior_vs_frequentist.md)
  : Side-by-side Bayesian vs frequentist headline table (Part D).

- [`variance_decomposition()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/variance_decomposition.md)
  : Decompose posterior variance into parameter vs evaluation-sample
  sources.

- [`bb_weights()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/bb_weights.md)
  :

  Generate a matrix of Bayesian-bootstrap weights `[S x n]` (rows sum to
  1).

- [`bb_replicates()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/bb_replicates.md)
  : Bayesian-bootstrap replicates of a metric on a SINGLE fixed
  prediction set.

- [`bb_optimism()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/bb_optimism.md)
  : Bayesian-bootstrap optimism correction for a scalar validation
  metric.

## Discrimination metrics

- [`metric_harrell_c()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_harrell_c.md)
  : Harrell's C (per draw). Wraps survival::concordance with case
  weights.

- [`metric_uno_c()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_uno_c.md)
  : Uno's C (IPCW, truncated at tau) per draw. survival::concordance
  with timewt = "n/G2" is the Uno estimator; ymax = tau truncates.

- [`metric_gonen_k()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_gonen_k.md)
  :

  Gonen-Heller K (per draw) — model-based concordance from eta only, so
  it is independent of the study censoring distribution. Closed form
  (A1):
  `K = sum_{i!=j} w_i w_j I(eta_i > eta_j) / (1 + exp(eta_j - eta_i))`
  normalised by the pair weight mass. O(n^2); intended for moderate n.

- [`metric_antolini_c()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_antolini_c.md)
  : Antolini's time-dependent concordance (per draw) — A1.4. Uses the
  model's time-specific survival: a usable pair (i event at Ytilde_i, j
  later) is concordant when S_i(Ytilde_i) \< S_j(Ytilde_i), i.e. the
  subject who failed had the lower predicted survival AT THAT TIME. For
  a PH model this reduces to Harrell's C; for flexible / non-PH models
  whose curves may cross it is the natural single summary. Survival at
  the (arbitrary) event times is obtained by interpolating each
  subject's cumulative hazard across the horizon knots.

- [`metric_td_auc()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_td_auc.md)
  : Time-dependent (cumulative/dynamic) AUC at each horizon, IPCW, per
  draw. Cases: T_i \<= t & event; controls: T_j \> t. Uses the predicted
  risk 1 - S_i(t) as the marker and IPCW weights G-hat from the
  censoring KM.

## Calibration metrics

- [`metric_citl()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_citl.md)
  : Calibration-in-the-large at each horizon (per draw): mean predicted
  risk vs observed (weighted Kaplan-Meier) risk.

- [`metric_cal_slope()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_cal_slope.md)
  : Calibration slope (per draw): coefficient of a Cox model with eta as
  the sole covariate. slope \< 1 signals overfitting (van Houwelingen
  shrinkage).

- [`metric_ici()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_ici.md)
  : ICI / E50 / E90 at a horizon (per draw): mean / 50th / 90th
  percentile of \|pi_i(t) - pi_hat^cal_i(t)\| (Austin, Harrell & van
  Klaveren 2020).

- [`metric_dcalibration()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_dcalibration.md)
  :

  D-calibration (per draw) — A2.6, Haider et al. (JMLR 2020).
  Distributional calibration of the WHOLE predicted survival
  distribution, not one horizon: if the model is calibrated, u_i =
  S_i(T_i) is Uniform(0,1). Bin `[0,1]` into `bins` equal cells; an
  event contributes 1 to its cell, a censored subject (known only that
  its true u \< S_i(c_i)) spreads its unit mass uniformly over
  `[0, S_i(c_i)]` across cells. The Pearson statistic vs the expected
  count n/bins tests uniformity (chi-square, bins-1 df).

- [`ppc_calibration()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/ppc_calibration.md)
  : Posterior predictive calibration check at a horizon.

- [`plot_calibration_band()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/plot_calibration_band.md)
  : Plot a posterior calibration band from ppc_calibration() (ggplot2).

## Overall performance

- [`metric_brier()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_brier.md)
  : IPCW Brier score at each horizon (per draw). BS(t) = sum_i w_i \*
  Ŵ_i(t) \* (I(Ytilde_i \> t) - S_i(t))^2 Ŵ_i(t): 1/G(T_i-) for events
  before t, 1/G(t) for survivors past t, 0 for subjects censored before
  t.
- [`metric_ipa()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_ipa.md)
  : Index of Prediction Accuracy (scaled Brier) at each horizon (per
  draw): IPA(t) = 1 - BS_model(t) / BS_null(t), null = marginal
  Kaplan-Meier.
- [`metric_r2d()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/metric_r2d.md)
  : Royston-Sauerbrei R^2_D (per draw) — explained variation from the
  ordered linear predictor. D is the Cox coefficient on scaled normal
  rankit scores. R^2_D = (D^2/kappa^2) / (pi^2/6 + D^2/kappa^2), kappa =
  sqrt(8/pi).

## Decision curve

- [`net_benefit_draw()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/net_benefit_draw.md)
  : Net benefit across thresholds for a single draw.
- [`posterior_net_benefit()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/posterior_net_benefit.md)
  : Posterior net-benefit curves over draws (B6).
- [`plot_net_benefit()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/plot_net_benefit.md)
  : Plot posterior net-benefit bands from posterior_net_benefit()
  (ggplot2).

## Configuration

- [`bc_config()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/bc_config.md)
  : Get the framework configuration, with optional per-call overrides.
- [`bc_horizons()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/bc_horizons.md)
  : Resolve evaluation horizons from data (or return the configured
  horizons).
- [`bc_tau()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/bc_tau.md) :
  Resolve the truncation tau (largest horizon when cfg\$tau is NULL).

## Plot helpers

- [`bc_palette`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/bc_palette.md)
  : Okabe-Ito colourblind-safe palette. Pick series colours by name;
  never introduce ad-hoc colours. Reference/guide lines are grey (see
  below).

- [`theme_bayesval()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/theme_bayesval.md)
  : The house theme: theme_classic() with a top legend and bold facet
  strips.

- [`number_ticks()`](https://wmotte.github.io/bayesval/reference/number_ticks.md)
  :

  pretty()-based axis ticks. Use as
  `scale_*_continuous(breaks = number_ticks(6))`.
